subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Should this remain the canonical local-vLLM timeout cascade tracker until a current-main live trace isolates the remaining bottleneck, or should maintainers split the remaining symptoms into narrower concurrency, gateway-deadlock, and provider-timeout trackers?
rationale: The issue spans provider timeouts, fallback semantics, cron/live-session behavior, auth-profile state, and gateway RPC availability, and current main only proves partial fixes rather than a single remaining implementation target.

options.title: Keep as canonical live-repro tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main local-vLLM trace before choosing the next code change.

options.title: Split by observed bottleneck
options.body: Use this issue as context and move remaining work to narrower issues once live logs identify provider timeout, gateway backpressure, or session-lock deadlock as the active cause.

options.title: Close only after proof
options.body: Treat the landed fixes as sufficient only if a current-main run shows the original false-timeout and `sessions_spawn` cascade no longer occurs.

recommendation.title: Keep as canonical live-repro tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main local-vLLM trace before choosing the next code change.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to osolmaz and the adjacent provider-auth startup fix was automerge-requested by osolmaz, making them the best available owner for triage direction.
